claims.text: The starting HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy is single phase.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
An optimized post-fabrication aging treatment can produce a fine, uniform dispersion of nanoscale coherent precipitates, such as B2 or L12 phases, in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Uniformly dispersed precipitates can improve high-strain-rate mechanical performance, whereas aggregated or large precipitates can degrade it.
Coherent nanoscale precipitates will obstruct dislocation glide in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Obstructing dislocation motion will increase dynamic work-hardening capacity.
The precipitate obstacle network will distribute dynamic deformation more uniformly.
The precipitate-strengthened microstructure will delay adiabatic shear-band formation and shear localization.
Aging will increase the alloy's dynamic yield and compressive strengths by approximately 10–20% relative to the untreated baseline.
Aging will increase uniform elongation and fracture strain under high-strain-rate loading.
Aging will enhance resistance to shear localization under high-strain-rate deformation.
The precipitates will moderate or improve control of impact-induced energy release.
The predicted benefits apply under approximately 10^3–10^4 s^-1 adiabatic dynamic loading.
The benefits may be lost if precipitate size, volume fraction, or spatial distribution is not optimized.
Coarsening of the precipitates may cause embrittlement.
Matched as-cast and aged HfZrTiTa0.53 specimens will be compared by dynamic compression or split-Hopkinson pressure-bar testing at 10^3–10^4 s^-1.
Failure to obtain statistically significant strength, elongation, and localization improvements, or observation of premature failure, will falsify the hypothesis.
